newsitem.title: USA: CardioGenesis sees estimates within range.
newsitem.headline: CardioGenesis sees estimates within range.

text.p: CardioGenesis Corp Chief Financial Officer Richard Powers said Thursday that analyst estimates of a $0.29 a share loss for second quarter and a $1.19 loss for 1997 are within the company's expectations.
"Our first quarter loss (of $0.30 a share) was in line with the way I think it (the company) will be performing," Powers told Reuters at a Piper Jaffray investors conference here.
"The projections that Piper Jaffray have (for the second quarter and full year) seem to be in the range," he said.

CardioGenesis Chief Executive Officer Allen Hill told investors at the conference that Boston Scientific Corp had committed 16 sales representatives exclusively for the company's products in Europe. Boston Scientific, a medical device company, has the exclusive rights to market CardioGenesis equipment.
"It (sales force) is in place in the major markets across Europe," he said.

Hill also said CardioGenesis plans to file its pre-market application late this year or very early in 1998 with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its ITMR (Interoperative Transmyocardial Revascularization) system. The ITMR is used to treat angina by using lasers to create channels in oxygen-deprived regions of the heart.
While the company is not being reimbursed by the U.S. Healthcare Financing Administration during clinical trials, Hill said that the company expected reimbursement once the products reach the market.

"It looks very good that the procedures will classify as 'Other Cardiovascular Procedures' which reimburse on average $25,000," Hill said. "The cost for the procedure will be $11,000 to $15,000, so there will be ample incentive for institutions to adopt this procedure."
